children.value: Here’s what our teaching approach is built on:
No tedious drilling. Unlike many typing tutors, KeyLearn never makes you repeat the same block like ‘
’ over and over. That gets tiresome fast and barely helps you learn.

Instead, an algorithm builds lessons that match your current skill level. Each lesson is made of random words drawn from a subset of your alphabet’s letters. The algorithm decides how large that subset is and how often each letter shows up, aiming to give you the most effective learning experience.

Letters quietly fade if you leave them alone

Skills rust when they go unused, and KeyLearn reflects that honestly. A key you haven't practiced in a long time slowly loses a little confidence over real time, so you might see an old letter drift back from green toward red on its own. That's not you getting worse — it's the app gently flagging that the letter is due for a refresh before it truly slips. Your best-ever result for a key is never wiped out; only the current reading softens.

xlxLJra+.value: While you’re focused on a new key, your speed on earlier keys will often dip a little. With this option off, a key unlocks as soon as the one you’re focusing on clears the target speed. With it on, every previously unlocked key must also stay above the target speed before a new one unlocks — harder to progress, but it also helps keep you from losing your grip on older keys.

y8v2PQLa.value: The classic touch-typing course: a fixed, finger-by-finger march through the keyboard — home row first, then the top and bottom rows. Familiar if you learned on TypingClub or Mavis Beacon. The one twist is that it’s adaptive — the next stage unlocks only once you’ve mastered the keys you’re on.
